items.title: Fix: Wait for Pages Router hydration before rendering route changes
items.body:
### What?

Fixes a Pages Router race condition where a route change requested before the initial hydration render starts ends up performing that hydration with the next page's props, resulting in a hydration mismatch

Fixes #95367

### Why?

`hydrate()` in `client/index.tsx` creates the router, which makes `window.next.router` usable right away. The initial render only starts after a few more awaits: `router._initialMatchesMiddlewarePromise`, and in development `beforeRender` (`displayContent` in `client/dev/fouc.ts`), which waits for `requestAnimationFrame`.

If `router.push()` is called in that window and its data loads first, the router's `subscription` calls `render()` for the new route. No React root exists yet, so `renderReactElement` calls `hydrateRoot` with the new page's element against the old page's HTML.

Development makes the window much wider. Chrome doesn't run animation frames in background tabs, so a background tab never starts its initial render. That's what the issue's repro encounters. That also explains why one tab or `page.goto()` doesn't reproduce it.

### How?

- `client/index.tsx`: route-change renders from the router's `subscription` and waits until the initial render settles (its promise resolves on commit, or rejects if the render is canceled or fails). The router state and URL update as before; only the render waits.
- `client/dev/fouc.ts`: `displayContent` already falls back to `setTimeout` in iframes because the animation frame may never fire. This extends that fallback to hidden documents. Without it, the change above makes navigations in a background dev tab wait until the tab becomes visible, because that tab's initial render never starts.

### Tests

Added `test/development/pages-dir/router-push-before-hydration`. It holds animation frames so the page stays in `beforeRender`, pushes `/b`, waits for the URL to change (the router does that after `/b`'s data loads, right before rendering), releases the frames, then checks that `/b` renders without a hydration error.

items.title: Catch-all route on Vercel: server-side `usePathname()` percent-encodes slashes (`/a%2Fb%2Fc`) for paths not returned by `generateStaticParams`

labels.name: Runtime
labels.description: Related to Node.js or Edge Runtime with Next.js.

items.body: ### Link to the code that reproduces this issue https://github.com/glenn-jocher/next-pathname-encoding-repro ### To Reproduce The app has one optional catch-all page with ISR and a partial `generateStaticParams`, plus a client component that prints `usePathname()`. `app/layout.tsx` is a plain `{children}` root layout. ```tsx // app/[[...slug]]/page.tsx import { Probe } from "../probe"; export const revalidate = 86400; export function generateStaticParams() { return [{ slug: [] }, { slug: ["pre", "rendered"] }]; } export default function Page() { return ; } ``` ```tsx // app/probe.tsx "use client"; import { usePathname } from "next/navigation"; export function Probe() { const pathname = usePathname(); return ( <> {pathname} login ); } ``` 1. Define a helper that prints the cache header, the server-rendered pathname, the link, and the canonical URL segments (`"c"`) from the inline RSC payload: ```bash probe() { curl -s -i "$1" | grep -oE '^x-vercel-cache: [A-Z]+|[^<]*|/a/b/c /pre/rendered # prerendered probe https:///a/b/c # on demand probe https:///x/y # on demand ``` ``` x-vercel-cache: HIT /pre/rendered /a%2Fb%2Fc /x%2Fy /a/b/c`) has the same `"c":["","a%2Fb%2Fc"]`. 4. Open `https:///a/b/c` in a browser: React throws minified error #418 (hydration text mismatch), then the client re-renders with `/a/b/c`. ### Current vs. Expected behavior **Current (Vercel):** for a catch-all path that `generateStaticParams` did not return, the on-demand server render puts the whole catch-all value into one percent-encoded canonical segment (`"c":["","a%2Fb%2Fc"]`), so server-side `usePathname()` returns `/a%2Fb%2Fc`. Values derived from it in the server HTML are wrong (`encodeURIComponent(pathname)` gives `%2Fa%252Fb%252Fc`), the wrong HTML is cached until revalidation, and hydration fails with #418. `params` is correct: `{"slug":["a","b","c"]}`. **Expected:** server-side `usePathname()` returns `/a/b/c`, as it does for prerendered paths, under `next start`, and on the client. Separate routes in one Vercel deployment, each requested at a path that was not prerendered: | Route | Request | Server `usePathname()` | |---|---|---| | `[[...slug]]` + `generateStaticParams` + `revalidate` | `/m/n/o` | `/m%2Fn%2Fo` (wrong) | | `[...slug]` + `generateStaticParams` + `revalidate` | `/req/m/n/o` | `/req/m%2Fn%2Fo` (wrong) | | `[[...slug]]` + `generateStaticParams`, no `revalidate` | `/ssg/m/n/o` | `/ssg/m%2Fn%2Fo` (wrong) | | `[[...slug]]` + `revalidate`, no `generateStaticParams` (built as dynamic) | `/isr/m/n/o` | `/isr/m/n/o` (correct) | | `[[...slug]]` + `dynamic = "force-dynamic"` | `/dyn/m/n/o` | `/dyn/m/n/o` (correct) | | `[a]/[b]` + `generateStaticParams` + `revalidate` | `/one/m/n` | `/one/m/n` (correct) | ### Provide environment information ``` Operating System: Platform: darwin Arch: arm64 Version: Darwin Kernel Version 27.0.0: Tue Aug 11 21:06:40 PDT 2026; root:xnu-13432.1.9~1/RELEASE_ARM64_T6050 Available memory (MB): 49152 Available CPU cores: 18 Binaries: Node: 26.5.1 npm: 11.17.0 Yarn: N/A pnpm: 10.26.2 Relevant Packages: next: 16.4.2 // Latest available version is detected (16.4.2). eslint-config-next: N/A react: 19.3.1 react-dom: 19.3.1 typescript: 7.0.2 Next.js Config: output: N/A ``` Deployed on Vercel (Node.js 24.x, default Turbopack build). Also reproduces with `next@16.5.0-canary.17` deployed to Vercel. ### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply) Dynamic Routes, Navigation, Runtime ### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply) Vercel (Deployed) ### Additional context - Local `next build && next start` is correct for every path above, including the RSC response. - Related but separate: #95648 (on Vercel, the root route's server-side `usePathname()` is `/index`; fix in #95973). That fix normalizes only the root `/index` case. In this repro the root `/` is correct (`"c":["",""]`). - Guess (unverified): on Vercel the fallback render receives the catch-all value as one string (`a/b/c`) and builds the canonical URL by encoding it as a single segment. `"c"` has one element for three path segments.

items.title: Turbopack (App Router): route react-loadable-manifest names an unemitted chunk when a layout's next/dynamic gate is also reached from the page (preload 404)

labels.name: Lazy Loading
labels.description: Related to Next.js Lazy Loading (e.g., next/dynamic or React.lazy).

items.body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/ysfsarikaya/next-turbopack-loadable-manifest-repro

### To Reproduce

1. `git clone https://github.com/ysfsarikaya/next-turbopack-loadable-manifest-repro && cd next-turbopack-loadable-manifest-repro`
2. `./reproduce.sh canary` (or `./reproduce.sh` for the pinned `next@16.3.4`). It installs, runs `next build`, runs `check-manifest.mjs` (compares every route's `react-loadable-manifest.json` with `.next/static/chunks`), starts `next start` on port 3999 and prints the script preloads of `/a` and `/b` with their HTTP status.

Or manually: `pnpm install && npx next build && npx next start`, open http://localhost:3000/b and look for a 404 on `/_next/static/chunks/*.js` in the Network tab.

Setup (App Router, no config, no dependencies besides next/react):

```
app/layout.tsx        renders <Gate />
app/a/page.tsx        nothing route-specific
app/b/page.tsx        renders <OnlyB /> and <Gate /> again
components/Gate.tsx   'use client'; const Heavy = dynamic(() => import('./Heavy').then(m => ({ default: m.Heavy })))
components/OnlyB.tsx  'use client'; import { Heavy } from './Heavy'   // static import of the gate's async target
components/Heavy.tsx  'use client'; ~30 KB inert payload so it gets its own chunk
```

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current** (16.5.0-canary.15): the per-route manifest of `/b` names a chunk that is never emitted, so the SSR HTML of `/b` preloads a 404:

```
ok       app/_not-found/page  40884  static/chunks/0ux4-jlr--gck.js
ok       app/a/page           40884  static/chunks/0ux4-jlr--gck.js
MISSING  app/b/page           40884  static/chunks/1nahbtiww_lu9.js

-- /b
<link rel="preload" href="/_next/static/chunks/1nahbtiww_lu9.js" as="script" fetchPriority="low"/>
404  /_next/static/chunks/1nahbtiww_lu9.js
```

The only emitted loader for `import('./Heavy')` lives in the layout's chunk and points at the chunk `/a` lists (16.3.4 build):

```js
83467,e=>{e.v(t=>Promise.all(["static/chunks/2legknbp6gahp.js"].map(t=>e.l(t))).then(()=>t(40884)))}
```

In the browser, `/b` logs `Failed to load resource: 404` for `1nahbtiww_lu9.js`; after hydration the loader fetches `2legknbp6gahp.js` (200), which was not preloaded. The page renders and works; the cost is a 404 on every SSR of that route and a later-resolving `next/dynamic` island.

**Expected:** the manifest of `/b` lists the chunk the emitted loader requests (as it does for `/a`), so every preloaded chunk exists.

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: darwin
  Arch: arm64
  Version: Darwin Kernel Version 27.0.0
  Available memory (MB): 16384
  Available CPU cores: 8
Binaries:
  Node: 25.0.0
  npm: 11.11.0
  Yarn: 1.22.22
  pnpm: 10.33.2
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.5.0-canary.15
  eslint-config-next: N/A
  react: 19.3.0
  react-dom: 19.3.0
  typescript: 5.9.3
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Turbopack, Lazy Loading

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next build (local), next start (local)

### Additional context

Also reproduces on 16.3.4 and 16.4.2. Does not reproduce with `next build --webpack` (its manifest names an emitted chunk).

All three ingredients are needed; removing any one gives consistent output:

| Gate rendered by layout | Gate also reached from page `/b` | `/b` statically imports `Heavy` | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | yes | yes | manifest names an unemitted chunk |
| yes | yes | no  | consistent |
| yes | no  | yes | consistent (manifest = layout's chunk) |
| no  | yes | yes | consistent (`/b` gets its own loader and emitted chunk) |

This looks like the App Router counterpart of the Pages Router `/_app` case discussed in #99149 and fixed by #100091: the loader of `import('./Heavy')` is created in the layout's chunk group with the layout's availability, while the page's manifest resolves the same import with the page's availability, where `Heavy` is already in the entry, so it names a facade-only variant that is never emitted. #100091 says App Router is untouched, and canary.15 (which contains it) still reproduces. #99150 targets the `in_async_module()` mismatch, which is a different path.

items.title: docs: Clarify when useSearchParams boundaries render on the server with Cache Components
items.body:
## Summary

The `useSearchParams` docs say a prerendered route client-renders the tree up to the closest `<Suspense>` boundary. With Cache Components, that only holds when the rest of the route is prerendered. If any component on the route reads request data, such as `cookies()`, the postponed boundary is rendered on the server at request time with the real search params. Code inside it then runs on the server, and browser-only reads in render cause hydration mismatches.

- `docs/01-app/03-api-reference/04-functions/use-search-params.mdx`: In Prerendering, state when the boundary is server-rendered under Cache Components, and point to `use(browser())` for browser-only components.
- `errors/blocking-prerender-client-hook.mdx`: The Trade-off section said the fallback always swaps after hydration. Qualify it to routes where the rest is prerendered, and point to `use(browser())` for the request-time case.
- `docs/01-app/02-guides/instant-navigation.mdx`: "suspends during server rendering" to "suspends during prerendering".

Left unchanged: `errors/missing-suspense-with-csr-bailout.mdx`, which describes the non-Cache Components model and is accurate there.

Finding: https://next-maintainer-agent.vercel.tools/agent-feedback/2121

## Verification

Production build on `next@16.4.0-canary.37` with `cacheComponents: true`, `curl "/<route>?q=hello"`:

| Route | `useSearchParams` boundary in server HTML |
| --- | --- |
| Rest of the route prerendered | No, fallback only |
| `cookies()` in a sibling `<Suspense>` | Yes, with `hello` |
| `cookies()` awaited above the component | Yes, with `hello` |
| Sibling `cookies()`, component calls `use(browser())` | No, sibling still streams |

Matches `app-render.tsx`: a complete server result resumes and aborts postponed HTML boundaries into client render mode, a partial one saves postponed state for the request-time resume. Only `useSearchParams` was tested; the error page Trade-off covers the other URL hooks on the same code path.

<!-- NEXT_JS_LLM -->

items.title: Build the inline Flight script from React's strings instead of re-encoding them
items.body:
React's Flight server on Node writes two kinds of chunks:

- Short rows are UTF-8-encoded into a 4 KB buffer and written as bytes.
- Strings longer than about 1365 characters are [written as JS strings](https://github.com/facebook/react/blob/b618bbb4/packages/react-server/src/ReactServerStreamConfigNode.js#L61-L72), leaving the encoding to the consumer.

A row is one line, `id:<json>`, and React [builds it as a single string](https://github.com/facebook/react/blob/b618bbb4/packages/react-server/src/ReactFlightServer.js#L4793-L4795). So a row with 1365+ characters of JSON is written as a string too. Pages with a lot of markup and few Suspense boundaries are mostly such rows.

## Before

`renderToNodeFlightStream` piped React into `new PassThrough()`, a byte-mode stream. Node encodes every string written to a byte-mode stream, so each of those strings became a Buffer on the way in. Both consumers then decoded it: `createFromNodeStream` for SSR, and the inline-data writer, which did this for each chunk to build the `__next_f` script:

```js
const decodedString = chunk.toString('utf-8')
htmlInlinedData = htmlEscapeJsonString(JSON.stringify([1, decodedString]))
output.push(Buffer.from(`<script>self.__next_f.push(${htmlInlinedData})</script>`))
```

## After

The stream is object mode, so the strings reach the consumers as strings. The inline writer escapes them straight into the script. SSR reads them directly, which React's reader [supports](https://github.com/facebook/react/blob/b618bbb4/packages/react-client/src/ReactFlightClient.js#L5500-L5508). Prerender capture, byte counting, Web stream conversion and the HTTP response still need bytes and encode for themselves.

## Numbers

`sandbox-bench`: 16 fresh VMs per experiment, each running both arms twice, interleaved. Cells are the 95% range across VMs; bold is p < 0.01.

Each commit against the one before it. `/streaming/heavy` has 240 boundaries, each with a 3 KB string prop and a 1.5 KB text node. `/streaming/heavy-unicode` (added in this PR) is the same with one non-Latin-1 character in each string, which makes V8 store them at two bytes per character.

| Commit | `heavy` median | `heavy-unicode` median | `heavy-unicode` throughput, 8 clients |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Switch the stream to object mode | no change | −4% to 0% | no change |
| Escape inline strings without decoding | −7% to 0% | **−15% to −11%** | **+17% to +26%** |
| Encode fragments into one Buffer | −15% to 0% | **−20% to −6%** | **+8% to +38%** |
| All three | **−16% to −6%** | **−28% to −19%** | **+21% to +42%** |

The inline writer can only skip the decode once it receives strings, which is what the first commit provides. On its own that commit also removes the SSR decode and adds the `toWellFormed()` scan, and those roughly cancel. The next two commits remove the decode and re-encode in the inline writer.

The whole PR by route. The app routes were measured twice, on new VMs.

| Route | Median latency, 1 client | Throughput, 8 clients |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/streaming/heavy` | **−16% to −6%** | **+19% to +38%** |
| `/streaming/heavy-unicode` | **−28% to −19%** | **+21% to +42%** |
| `/blog` | **−14% to −7%** | **+11% to +24%** |
| `/blog`, repeated | **−15% to −5%** | **+8% to +23%** |
| `/docs` | **−15% to −9%** | **+8% to +44%** |
| `/docs`, repeated | −14% to −2% | +1% to +20% |
| `/dashboard` | −11% to −1% | **+6% to +22%** |
| `/dashboard`, repeated | no change | **+9% to +32%** |

TTFB moves with the median. `/streaming/chunkstorm` (1 KB strings) and `/streaming/bulk` (384-byte rows) have no strings over the threshold and did not move in any commit. `heavy-unicode` checks whether `toWellFormed()`, which scans two-byte strings, has a measurable cost. The two-byte route improves more than the one-byte route, because encoding and decoding two-byte strings is more expensive to begin with, so whatever the scan costs is small compared to what the other two commits remove. In CPU profiles, `utf8Write` (the encode) is down 48%, `Buffer#toString` (the writer's decode) down 94%, `TextDecoder` (the SSR decode) about 65%. Memory is not recorded by this harness.

<details>
<summary>All cells</summary>

Change with 95% range across the 16 VMs of each experiment. Bold is p < 0.01; "no change" means the range includes zero.

| Route | Median latency, 1 client | TTFB, 1 client | Median latency, 8 clients | Throughput, 8 clients |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `/streaming/heavy` | **−11.0% (−16.3 to −5.7)** | **−15.4% (−19.7 to −11.1)** | **−17.0% (−25.7 to −8.3)** | **+28.4% (+18.8 to +38.0)** |
| `/streaming/heavy-unicode` | **−23.3% (−27.7 to −18.9)** | **−27.8% (−32.4 to −23.2)** | **−20.6% (−27.5 to −13.7)** | **+31.4% (+20.6 to +42.2)** |
| `/blog` | **−10.3% (−13.5 to −7.1)** | **−12.7% (−15.8 to −9.6)** | **−13.3% (−18.5 to −8.1)** | **+17.8% (+11.2 to +24.4)** |
| `/blog`, repeated | **−10.0% (−14.8 to −5.2)** | **−11.6% (−17.0 to −6.2)** | −10.7% (−19.2 to −2.2) | **+15.5% (+7.7 to +23.3)** |
| `/docs` | **−11.9% (−15.2 to −8.6)** | **−13.9% (−17.2 to −10.6)** | no change (−25.2 to +0.4) | **+26.0% (+8.2 to +43.8)** |
| `/docs`, repeated | −8.2% (−14.4 to −2.0) | **−10.3% (−16.7 to −3.9)** | no change (−14.4 to +7.2) | +10.6% (+1.3 to +19.9) |
| `/dashboard` | −5.5% (−10.5 to −0.5) | −6.9% (−13.5 to −0.3) | −9.3% (−16.5 to −2.1) | **+13.9% (+6.1 to +21.7)** |
| `/dashboard`, repeated | no change (−8.4 to +2.8) | no change (−12.0 to +3.0) | **−12.2% (−19.7 to −4.7)** | **+20.3% (+8.8 to +31.8)** |
| `/streaming/chunkstorm` | no change (−7.4 to +1.4) | no change (−8.2 to +0.8) | no change (−13.1 to +7.5) | no change (−2.8 to +20.8) |
| `/streaming/bulk` | no change (−6.2 to +2.2) | no change (−6.3 to +2.3) | no change (−8.0 to +10.2) | no change (−5.9 to +13.5) |

</details>

## Output is unchanged

- **HTML bytes.** Identical between arms on every bench route. A unit test checks the inline script bytes for mixed string and byte input, including UTF-8 split across chunks and `</script` split across strings.
- **Lone surrogates.** A JS string can contain half of a surrogate pair. UTF-8 cannot represent it, so encoding replaces it with U+FFFD. Before, everything was encoded, so SSR, the inline script and the RSC response all showed U+FFFD. Now SSR would see the original character while the client still sees U+FFFD, a hydration mismatch. So the stream runs each string through `toWellFormed()`, which replaces lone surrogates with U+FFFD the same way. The e2e test checks all three agree and that hydration logs no mismatch.
- **`res.write`.** Custom servers still receive Buffers; the response pipe converts strings before writing. An e2e with a custom server checks this in dev and production, with and without cache components.

<details>
<summary>Verification</summary>

- Unit: `test/unit/inline-flight-data.test.ts`. Exact inline script bytes for mixed string and byte input at three sizes; UTF-8 split across adjacent byte chunks; byte views with a nonzero offset; `</script` split across string chunks.
- E2E `test/e2e/app-dir/flight-native-chunks`: `test-start-turbo`, `test-dev-turbo`, `test-start-webpack`.
- E2E `test/e2e/app-dir/custom-server-response-chunks`: same three, plus start and dev with the cache-components env. Rebuilding without the response-boundary conversion makes its RSC case fail with `string` and `uint8array` chunks, so the test does see Next's writes. Compression is off in the fixture; with it on, the server only sees gzip's output.
- `test/e2e/app-dir/rsc-basic` under `test-start-turbo`.
- `pnpm --filter=next types`, prettier, eslint.

Bench cells: `pr100142-stress` (streaming routes; base is the bench-route commit, cand is head), `pr100142-realistic` and `pr100142-realistic-confirm` (`/blog,/dashboard,/docs`, same arms), `pr100142-buffer` (last commit against its parent, streaming routes).

</details>
